hotspots.whyItMatters: Egress lighting and exit-sign power tie directly into electrical rough-in on commercial jobs.
hotspots.cite: NFPA 101 — Means of Egress chapter (confirm chapter number in your 2018 edition)
hotspots.trap: Treating 'emergency lighting' and 'exit sign illumination' as one single requirement instead of two separate duties with separate duration/level rules.

hotspots.whyItMatters: The electrical scope for life-safety branch circuits depends on these performance numbers.
hotspots.cite: NFPA 101 — Emergency Lighting section (confirm section number in your edition)
hotspots.trap: Sizing an emergency lighting unit for initial illumination only and ignoring the required minimum level at the end of the duration period.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Nearly every other Life Safety Code requirement (egress capacity, alarm requirement) is keyed off occupancy classification.
hotspots.cite: NFPA 101 — Classification of Occupancy chapter (confirm chapter number in your edition)
hotspots.trap: Picking an occupancy classification by the building's general use instead of the code's specific occupant-load and use-condition tests.

hotspots.topic: Fire alarm and detection requirements by occupancy
hotspots.whyItMatters: Cross-references NFPA 72 requirements back into a specific occupancy chapter.
hotspots.cite: NFPA 101 — the relevant occupancy chapter (confirm chapter in your edition); cross-check NFPA 72
hotspots.trap: Applying a fire-alarm requirement found in one occupancy chapter to a different occupancy without checking that chapter's own rule.
